lines.text: Stock delisted? Delisting alone doesn't erase your shares.
lines.say: Stock delisted? Delisting alone doesn't erase your shares.

lines.text: You still own them. They often trade over the counter, with fewer buyers and wider spreads.

lines.text: Some delistings are voluntary, like cash buyouts. Others are forced out.

lines.text: On Nasdaq, a closing bid under $1 for 30 straight business days starts a 180-day fix-it clock.

lines.text: A common fix: a reverse split. Say 10 fifty-cent shares become 1 five-dollar share.

post.title: Delisting alone doesn't erase your shares
post.ig:
Stock delisted? Delisting alone doesn't erase your shares.
Delisted stocks often keep trading over the counter, with fewer buyers and wider spreads.
Nasdaq: a closing bid under $1 for 30 business days in a row brings a warning and usually 180 days to fix it.
Since 2025, no grace period if the company did a reverse split in the past year.
The real risk is bankruptcy: the SEC says a bankrupt company's common stock is likely worthless. The original Bed Bath & Beyond's shares were canceled in September 2023.
Sources: SEC investor bulletin, Nasdaq rules, Federal Register, the original Bed Bath & Beyond's 2023 Chapter 11 plan.
